prf:q-bessel-c-k-recurrence-cfinite:
Proof Throughout, q and the order \nu are formal parameters in a field; no archimedean structure is used. Write (x;q)_k = \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1 - x q^{j}\bigr) for the q-Pochhammer symbol, with (x;q)_0 = 1.

Step 1 — the closed-form coefficients and their ratio. The Hahn–Exton q-Bessel function of order \nu has power-series coefficients

c_k \;=\; \frac{(-1)^k\, q^{k(k-1)/2}}{(q;q)_k\,\bigl(q^{\nu+1};q\bigr)_k}, \qquad k \ge 0 .

Compare consecutive coefficients. The sign contributes a factor -1; the Gaussian exponent contributes q^{k(k+1)/2 - k(k-1)/2} = q^{k}; and each q-Pochhammer symbol gains exactly one factor,

\frac{(q;q)_{k+1}}{(q;q)_k} = 1 - q^{k+1},
\qquad
\frac{\bigl(q^{\nu+1};q\bigr)_{k+1}}{\bigl(q^{\nu+1};q\bigr)_k} = 1 - q^{\nu+k+1}.

Multiplying out, the coefficients satisfy the first-order q-recurrence

c_{k+1}\,\bigl(1 - q^{k+1}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k+1}\bigr) \;=\; -\,q^{k}\, c_k
\qquad (\star)

for all k \ge 0.

Step 2 — first-order recurrences integrate to a product. Conversely, (\star) determines the sequence from its seed. Let (r_k)_{k \ge 0} be any sequence of scalars and suppose a sequence (c_k) satisfies c_{k+1} = r_k\, c_k for all k. Then, by induction on k,

c_k \;=\; c_0 \prod_{j=0}^{k-1} r_j ,

the empty product being 1 at k = 0 and the induction step reading c_{k+1} = r_k\, c_k = c_0 \prod_{j=0}^{k} r_j. For generic parameters the denominators \bigl(1 - q^{k+1}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k+1}\bigr) never vanish (vanishing requires q a root of unity or q^{\nu+1} \in q^{-\mathbb{N}}), so (\star) is of this form with ratio

r_k \;=\; \frac{-\,q^{k}}{\bigl(1 - q^{k+1}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k+1}\bigr)} ,

and every solution of (\star) is the q-hypergeometric product c_k = c_0 \prod_{j=0}^{k-1} r_j. In particular the closed form of Step 1 is the unique solution with c_0 = 1.

Step 3 — q-holonomic, with C-finite as the degeneration. The ratio r_k depends on k through q^{k}: the recurrence (\star) is first-order linear with q^{k}-dependent coefficients, so the sequence (c_k) is q-holonomic. A constant-coefficient (C-finite) recurrence arises exactly in the degenerate case of a k-independent ratio: if c_{k+1} = \rho\, c_k for a single scalar \rho, the product of Step 2 collapses to the geometric sequence

c_k = c_0\, \rho^{k},

which is C-finite of order 1 with characteristic root \rho. This degeneration occurs in the rational limit of the underlying q-difference kernel (in particular after the q \to 1 contraction, where the rescaled ratio (1-q)^2\, c_{k+1}/c_k tends to -1/\bigl((k+1)(\nu+k+1)\bigr), the coefficient ratio of the classical Bessel series), never for the genuine q-Bessel ratio r_k.

Step 4 — consequence for the precision-ladder coefficients. At the fibre level the ladder kernel is a q-Bessel object, not a rational function; by Step 3 its coefficient sequence therefore admits no low-order constant-coefficient recurrence, while the dominant-root structure of the associated q-difference kernel survives. The canonical ladder values c_2, \ldots, c_{10}, expanded in the ladder variable u \approx 0.00852, exhibit exactly this pair of signatures: no constant-coefficient recurrence of order at most 4 fits them, while the tail ratio approaches the reciprocal pole location, c_{k+1}/c_k \to 1/u \approx 117.4. \blacksquare

This argument supplies the fibre-level skeleton of the recursion only: the identification of the ladder with a q-Bessel coefficient sequence is a formal statement in q and \nu, and the production c_k ladder remains calibration-anchored.
prf:q-bessel-second-order-qdifference:
Proof Throughout, q and the order \nu are formal parameters in a field; the argument is purely q-difference-algebraic. Write (x;q)_k = \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1 - x q^{j}\bigr) for the q-Pochhammer symbol, and let

g(w) \;=\; \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k\, w^{k},
\qquad
c_k \;=\; \frac{(-1)^k\, q^{k(k-1)/2}}{(q;q)_k\,\bigl(q^{\nu+1};q\bigr)_k},

be the generating function of the Hahn–Exton q-Bessel coefficients of order \nu. By the contiguity recurrence, the coefficients satisfy the first-order relation

c_k\,\bigl(1 - q^{k}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k}\bigr) \;=\; -\,q^{k-1}\, c_{k-1},
\qquad k \ge 1. \qquad (\star)

Step 1 — assemble the three q-shifts. The q-shifted series are g(qw) = \sum_{k} c_k\, q^{k} w^{k} and g(q^2 w) = \sum_{k} c_k\, q^{2k} w^{k}. Hence

q^{\nu}\, g(q^2 w) - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu}\bigr)\, g(q w) + g(w)
\;=\; \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k \Bigl( q^{\nu+2k} - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu}\bigr) q^{k} + 1 \Bigr) w^{k},

and the bracket factors,

q^{\nu+2k} - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu}\bigr) q^{k} + 1
\;=\; \bigl(1 - q^{k}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k}\bigr),

as one checks by expanding the right-hand side. This factorisation into the (\star) denominator is the reason the second-order operator collapses onto the first-order recurrence.

Step 2 — the source term. Re-indexing a single q-shift multiplied by w,

w\, g(q w) \;=\; \sum_{k \ge 0} c_k\, q^{k} w^{k+1} \;=\; \sum_{k \ge 1} c_{k-1}\, q^{k-1} w^{k}.

Step 3 — coefficient comparison. Combining Steps 1 and 2, the w^{k} coefficient of

q^{\nu}\, g(q^2 w) - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu} - w\bigr)\, g(q w) + g(w)

is c_0 \bigl(1 - q^{0}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu}\bigr) = 0 for k = 0, and

c_k\,\bigl(1 - q^{k}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k}\bigr) + q^{k-1}\, c_{k-1}

for k \ge 1. By (\star) every coefficient vanishes, so the generating function satisfies the second-order q-difference equation

q^{\nu}\, g(q^2 w) \;-\; \bigl(1 + q^{\nu} - w\bigr)\, g(q w) \;+\; g(w) \;=\; 0.
\qquad (\star\star)

Writing \eta for the q-shift operator (\eta f)(w) = f(qw), equation (\star\star) reads \bigl[\,q^{\nu}\eta^{2} - \bigl(1 + q^{\nu} - w\bigr)\eta + 1\,\bigr] g = 0: a genuine second-order (three-point: w, qw, q^2 w) q-difference operator, whose linear term +w in the middle coefficient is the source making the coefficient ladder descend.

Step 4 — equivalence of (\star\star) and (\star). The computation in Steps 1–3 is reversible: (\star\star) holds if and only if every w^{k} coefficient vanishes, and for k \ge 1 that vanishing is exactly (\star). The "second order" refers to the q-difference order (three q-shifted arguments); on the coefficients the equation collapses to a two-term relation between consecutive c_k, precisely because the middle coefficient factors through the (\star) denominator as in Step 1. Equivalently, shifting the index to k+1, the coefficient relation is

\Bigl( q^{\nu+2k+2} - q^{k+1} - q^{\nu+k+1} + 1 \Bigr) c_{k+1} + q^{k}\, c_k = 0,
\qquad
q^{\nu+2k+2} - q^{k+1} - q^{\nu+k+1} + 1 = \bigl(1 - q^{k+1}\bigr)\bigl(1 - q^{\nu+k+1}\bigr).

Step 5 — classical contraction. In the limit q \to 1^{-} the rescaled operator contracts to the ordinary Bessel operator w\, g'' + (\nu + 1)\, g' + g acting on g(w): the denominators degenerate as 1 - q^{k} \sim k\,(1-q) and 1 - q^{\nu+k} \sim (\nu+k)(1-q), so the rescaled coefficient ratio satisfies \lim_{q \to 1^{-}} (1-q)^{2}\, c_k / c_{k-1} = -1/\bigl(k(\nu+k)\bigr), the coefficient recurrence of the classical Bessel series \sum_{k} (-1)^k z^k / \bigl(k!\, (\nu+1)_k\bigr) in a formal variable z, where (\nu+1)_k is the ordinary Pochhammer symbol. \blacksquare

This is a fibre-level structural result: q and \nu are formal parameters, and no substrate evaluation is involved.

rem:qbeta-odd-carrier-hopf-cubic:
Remark The \mathfrak{Q}_\beta odd-channel obstruction is an irreducible cubic in the trace variable, sourced by the Hopf (double-crossing) sector. The precision-ladder coefficient c_3 splits under the bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} into a bar-even part (exactly measured) and a bar-odd part, the latter being the open channel. Its carrier is the bar-odd part of the net decay-width Laurent polynomial \Delta_{\mathrm{net}} = \Delta(\mathfrak{n}) - \Delta(\mathfrak{p}) on the \mathbf{H}_3 normal-form basis, whose numerator over 4q^7 is

\mathrm{num}(q) = q^{14} - 5q^{12} + 10q^{10} - 16q^{8} + 16q^{6} - 10q^{4} + 5q^{2} - 1.

The cyclotomic content factors cleanly into a quantum differential. Exactly, \mathrm{num}(q) = (q^2 - 1)\,R_{12}(q), which means the bar-odd part of the categorical net evaluates exactly to:

\Delta_{\mathrm{net}}^{\mathrm{odd}} = \frac{q - q^{-1}}{4} \cdot C(y) = \frac{h}{4} \cdot C(y)

where h = q - q^{-1} is the quantum differential and C(y) is a cubic in the bar-even loop-trace variable y = q^2 + q^{-2} = 2\cosh 2\lambda given by:

C(y) = y^3 - 4y^2 + 3y - 2.

C is irreducible over \mathbb{Q} (its only possible rational roots \pm 1, \pm 2 are all nonzero), so its root generates a genuine degree-3 field (discriminant -152 = -2^3 \cdot 19, Galois group S_3). Every substrate quadratic anchor sits at a rational trace value — golden \varphi \mapsto y = 3, silver 1 + \sqrt{2} \mapsto y = 6, classical q = 1 \mapsto y = 2 — and C is nonzero at each. A degree-\le 2 number can never be a root of an irreducible cubic, so no quadratic-anchor or real-q construction can reproduce the odd carrier: this is the structural reason the real-q c_3 closures fail.

The degree-3 comes from the Hopf (double-crossing) sector. Decomposing the bar-odd carrier over the knot sectors of the \mathbf{H}_3 normal form isolates the origin of the cubic:

knot sector crossings \Delta^{\mathrm{odd}}_{\mathrm{sector}}
virtual (\sigma_0, \sigma_1) 1 0
electron (\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0) 3 0
unknot (\mathbf{1}) 0 \frac{h}{4} \cdot (2y^2 - 7y + 4) = \frac{h}{4} \cdot C_{\mathrm{unknot}}(y)
L_\pm (\sigma_0\sigma_1 + \sigma_1\sigma_0) 2 \frac{h}{4} \cdot (y^3 - 6y^2 + 10y - 6) = \frac{h}{4} \cdot C_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(y)

with C = C_{\mathrm{Hopf}} + C_{\mathrm{unknot}}. The odd-crossing sectors (virtual, electron) are bar-even and vanish; the identity contributes only a quadratic; the cubic — hence the degree-3 field — is sourced entirely by the Hopf-link (double-crossing) sector. C_{\mathrm{Hopf}} is itself irreducible (discriminant -76 = -2^2 \cdot 19), and the prime 19 is the arithmetic fingerprint shared with the total C. So the obstruction is not a 3-dimensional representation (\mathbf{H}_3 has none — its Wedderburn blocks are 1, 2, 1) nor a single knot invariant, but the two-crossing isospin amplitude difference. Any genuine odd-channel closure must supply the cubic field of C_{\mathrm{Hopf}}, routed through the archimedean evaluation of the Markov crossing term, rather than a fibre-level real-q formula.
prop:faddeev-phib-uniqueness:
Proposition Uniqueness of the modular-double \Phi_b: strip growth pins the quantum dilogarithm up to scale. Conditional on the Faddeev shift-class and its strip-growth characterization. Fix the substrate parameter b = b(t) on the product-supported branch \mathrm{Im} b^2 > 0 (in particular the physical map b(t) = \sqrt{t/2\pi}\,e^{i\pi/4} with t = \ln q_0 > 0). Let \Phi_1 be any solution of the two modular-double q-difference equations of the non-compact quantum dilogarithm at b that is (i) comparable in modulus to the canonical product \Phi_b — some C > 0 bounds each of \lVert\Phi_1\rVert,\ \lVert\Phi_b\rVert by C times the other — and (ii) meromorphic on \mathbb{C} and continuous wherever \Phi_b \neq 0. Then \Phi_1 = c\,\Phi_b for a single constant c, on the nonvanishing locus of \Phi_b.

Here \Phi_b is the modular-double product

\Phi_b(z) \;=\;
\frac{\prod_{k\ge 0}\bigl(1 + e^{i\pi b^2(2k+1)}\,e^{2\pi b z}\bigr)}
     {\prod_{k\ge 0}\bigl(1 + e^{-i\pi b^{-2}(2k+1)}\,e^{2\pi z/b}\bigr)},

which on the branch \mathrm{Im} b^2 > 0 converges and equals the Faddeev contour integral. It is the canonical solution — it satisfies both hypotheses with c = 1, so the admissible class is nonempty and the constant is genuinely pinned.
prop:q-beta-c-2-eq-neg-one-structural:

prf:q-beta-c-2-eq-neg-one-structural:

prop:q-beta-bar-even-kernel-invariant:

conj:q-beta-radius-of-convergence-gate:

prop:q-beta-q-eq-one-shadow-gate:
Proposition \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder \S 4(c) formalize-first gate — any candidate Habiro element F(q) must reproduce the canonical integer shadows at q = 1: c_2 \to -1 (the structural N=2 anchor) and c_3 \to J_{\text{Hopf}}(1) = -2 (registry anchor); a candidate failing either is structurally REFUTED. prf:q-beta-q-eq-one-shadow-gate:
Proof Proof of q beta q eq one shadow gate. Let F(q) be a candidate Habiro element for the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision ladder, generating coefficient functions c_k(q) through its q-difference kernel (c_k recursion), so that the ladder correction reads \prod_{k \ge 2}\bigl(1 + c_k(q)\,u^k\bigr) with u = b(q)\,\hbar_q^2 the ladder variable. The gate asserts two classical shadows of the canonical ladder, \lim_{q \to 1} c_2(q) = -1 and \lim_{q \to 1} c_3(q) = -2, and refutes any candidate failing either. The proof establishes the two anchor values, then the rejection.

Step 1 — the c_2 shadow is exact at every q. By the c_2 structural identity, the operator-valued N = 2 correction of the canonical ladder factorises as the algebraic identity

1 + c_2\,u^2 \;=\; 1 - b(q)^2\,\hbar_q^4 \;=\; 1 - u^2 ,

valid over any commutative ring. Hence c_2(q) = -1 identically in q — a Taylor-exact constant, independent of q_0 and of all experimental input. The classical shadow \lim_{q \to 1} c_2(q) = -1 holds trivially, as the limit of a constant function.

Step 2 — the c_3 shadow equals J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(1) = -2. The canonical N = 3 correction is anchored, per the registry anchoring recorded in the statement, to the Jones polynomial of the Hopf link in the classical limit; at the value level for q \ne 1 the coefficient remains a near-match, which this gate does not use. It remains to evaluate J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(1). Work in the normalization J_{\mathrm{unknot}} = 1 with the skein relation J_{L_+} - J_{L_-} = (q - q^{-1})\,J_{L_0}.

  1. At q = 1 the right-hand side vanishes, so J_{L_+}(1) = J_{L_-}(1): the evaluation at q = 1 is invariant under crossing changes.
  2. Crossing changes transform any diagram of an n-component link into a diagram of the split union of n unknots, so J_L(1) depends only on the number of components n.
  3. In this normalization, adjoining a split unknotted component multiplies the invariant by the loop value -(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}), which at q = 1 equals -2; the unknot itself has value 1.

Hence J_L(1) = (-2)^{\,n-1} for every n-component link L. The Hopf link has n = 2 components, so J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(1) = -2, an exact integer. (Consistency check: the positive Hopf link has J(q) = -q^{1/2} - q^{5/2}, whose value at q = 1 is -2.)

Step 3 — the gate. The canonical ladder therefore satisfies c_2(1) = -1 (Step 1, exactly, at every q) and c_3(1) = -2 (Step 2, via the registry anchoring). Both anchors are integers evaluated at q = 1: the test lives entirely at the fibre level, involves no substrate anchor q_0, and admits no experimental tolerance — agreement is exact or it is not. Suppose a candidate F generates (c_2(q), c_3(q)) with c_2(1) \ne -1 or c_3(1) \ne -2. Then its coefficient functions disagree with the canonical ladder's at order u^2 or u^3 in the classical limit; since the c_k are determined by F through the q-difference kernel, F does not generate the canonical ladder. The candidate is structurally refuted before any anchor sweep at q_0 — the formalize-first rejection. \blacksquare
prop:order-of-magnitude-screen:
Proposition The order-of-magnitude screen \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x): monotone in the threshold, multiplicative, conditional rejection, finite-ladder bound, and the threshold-free direction obstruction. Let K be a linearly ordered field, \lambda\in K a threshold and t\in K with t\ge0 a target. An element x\in K passes the \lambda-screen at t, written \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x), if t\le\lambda|x| and |x|\le\lambda t. The additive band is \mathrm{Add}_\lambda(t,x): |x-t|\le\lambda t. Then:

  1. (Order structure.) For t\ge0: \lambda\le\lambda' and \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x) imply \mathrm{Scr}_{\lambda'}(t,x); \lambda\ge1 implies \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,t); \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x)\iff\mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,|x|)\iff\mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(|x|,t); for \lambda,\mu,b\ge0, \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(a,b) and \mathrm{Scr}_\mu(b,c) imply \mathrm{Scr}_{\lambda\mu}(a,c); and for a,b,c,d\ge0, \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(a,b) and \mathrm{Scr}_\mu(c,d) imply \mathrm{Scr}_{\lambda\mu}(ac,bd).
  2. (Conditional rejection.) Let \mu\le\lambda and t\ge0. If \mathrm{Scr}_\mu(t,x^\ast), then every x with \neg\mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x) satisfies x\ne x^\ast.
  3. (Finite ladder.) If s is finite and |a_k|\le\tfrac12 for k\in s, then \mathrm{Scr}_\Lambda\bigl(1,\prod_{k\in s}(1+a_k)\bigr) with \Lambda=\prod_{k\in s}(1+2|a_k|).
  4. (Direction obstruction, no threshold.) If 0\le z\le1, B\ge0 and B<t, then Bz^m<t for every m\in\mathbb N.
  5. (Upward closure.) If \lambda,B\ge0, 0\le z\le1, n\le m and \lambda Bz^n<t, then \neg\mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,Bz^m). If moreover K is Archimedean, 0\le z<1 and t>0, there is n with \neg\mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,Bz^m) for all m\ge n.
  6. (The additive band is one-sided.) If \lambda\ge1, t\ge0 and x\ge0, then \mathrm{Add}_\lambda(t,x)\iff x\le(\lambda+1)t; in particular \mathrm{Add}_\lambda(t,0) holds. For x\ge0, \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x) implies \mathrm{Add}_\lambda(t,x). For signed x the test |x-t|>\lambda t does not imply \neg\mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x): take t=1, \lambda=10, x=-19/2.
prf:order-of-magnitude-screen:
Proof Proof of the order-of-magnitude screen properties. Item 1. Multiply \lambda\le\lambda' by |x|\ge0 and by t\ge0. Reflexivity: t\le\lambda t for \lambda\ge1, t\ge0. The predicate depends on x only through |x|, and with |t|=t the two conjuncts swap under t\leftrightarrow|x|. Transitivity: a\le\lambda b\le\lambda\mu|c| and |c|\le\mu b\le\mu\lambda a. Products: multiply the inequalities, all factors being nonnegative.

Item 2. If x=x^\ast, item 1 lifts \mathrm{Scr}_\mu(t,x^\ast) to \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x).

Item 3. For y=|a|\le\tfrac12: 1+a\ge1-y\ge\tfrac12, 1+a\le1+2y, and (1+2y)(1+a)\ge(1+2y)(1-y)=1+y(1-2y)\ge1. So \mathrm{Scr}_{1+2y}(1,1+a), and the product rule of item 1 gives the finite product, the empty product being \mathrm{Scr}_1(1,1).

Item 4. 0\le z^m\le1, so Bz^m\le B<t.

Item 5. z^m\le z^n for m\ge n, so t\le\lambda Bz^m would give t\le\lambda Bz^n<t. In the Archimedean case choose n with z^n<t/(\lambda B+1); then \lambda Bz^n\le(\lambda B+1)z^n<t.

Item 6. |x-t|\le\lambda t is x-t\le\lambda t and t-x\le\lambda t; the second holds automatically for x\ge0, \lambda\ge1. For the counterexample, |-19/2|=19/2 lies in [1/10,10], while |-19/2-1|=21/2>10.

All items hold over any linearly ordered field; the eventual statement in item 5 additionally needs the field to be Archimedean.

The passage from item 3 to the infinite ladder \prod_{k\ge2}(1+c_ku_0^k) needs 1+y\le e^y (analysis) and the convergence of \sum_k|c_k|u_0^k, which is not proved. \blacksquare
rem:q-beta-direction-sanity-gate:
Remark \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder \S 4(d) formalize-first gate — any candidate Habiro element F(q_0) must have magnitude consistent with the target observable's order of magnitude; the z(q_0) \approx 0.6127 < 1 direction obstruction is the canonical refutation precedent. Any candidate Habiro element F(q) must satisfy the direction-sanity invariant: |F(q_0)| must be in the same order of magnitude as the target ratio \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^{\text{CODATA}} / [Q_A(q_0) \cdot \cos(\alpha_{\text{eff}}(q_0))]. A candidate predicting a magnitude differing by more than 10\times is screened out.

This is a magnitude check applied before any wide numerical search. This is an order-of-magnitude screen, not a structural exclusion: no proved invariant forbids a candidate outside the window, so a screened-out candidate is not refuted. The target is \approx 1 on the retired z = 1 base and \approx 1.76 on the canonical z = q^3/(q^2+1) base.

The screen is the predicate \mathrm{Scr}_{10}(t,|F(q_0)|) of The order-of-magnitude screen \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x), with the threshold 10 (one decade each way) a convention and the target t a comparison value. Everything provable about the gate is in that proposition. In particular a larger threshold only admits more candidates (item 1); a screen-out implies F\ne F_{\mathrm{true}} only if the true kernel passes the screen (item 2), which is a comparison with data; and the obstruction behind the canonical precedent, a candidate of the form B\,z(q_0)^m with 0\le z(q_0)\le1, needs no threshold (item 4): if B<t then B\,z(q_0)^m<t for every m. Whether B<t holds is again a comparison with data, and it fails on the retired z=1 base, where t<1. The additive band |m-t|\le10t, an alternative form of the gate, is not this window: on nonnegative magnitudes it is the one-sided bound m\le11t, so it rejects no too-small candidate (item 6).

sec:qbeta-formalize-first-gates-intro:
Because the Frobenius collapse T_\beta = S\cdot\mathbf{1} (Min-Frobenius-norm collapse: T_β = S · 1 under the canonical Markov-trace inner product on H_n(R, q)) reduces the leading \beta-decay amplitude on H_3(q) to a scalar, the sub-leading precision coefficients c_k of the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta ladder (Complex-Volume Precision Ladder) must arise from a fibre-level Habiro kernel F(q). Rather than searching unconstrained rational expressions for c_k, this section establishes the algebraic invariance gates that any candidate kernel F(q) must satisfy over \mathbb{Q}(q) prior to archimedean evaluation:

  1. Classical vanishing and shadow gate: In the classical limit q \to 1, the ratio \mathfrak{Q}_\beta/E_0 vanishes while the normalized Taylor shadows reproduce c_2 \to -1 and c_3 \to J_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(1) = -2 (S(q) = \mathfrak{Q}_\beta(q)/E_0(q) vanishes at the classical point q = 1, \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder \S 4(c) shadow gate).
  2. Bar-even kernel invariance: The kernel modifying the bar-odd carrier must itself be bar-even under q \mapsto q^{-1} so that the expansion proceeds in integer powers of u = b\,\hbar_q^2 (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder \bar{}-even discriminant).
  3. Habiro q-difference and Jackson q-Bessel recursion: Any kernel in the Habiro ring satisfies a finite-order q-difference equation, inducing a C-finite contiguity recurrence on c_k bridged to the per-block z-recursion (c_k precision-ladder recursion induced by the fibre-level Habiro q-difference equation, Bridge: z-Taylor recursion vs c_k ladder recursion — structural correspondence).
  4. Radius-of-convergence and magnitude screens: The kernel's singularity locus and sign pattern are constrained by the radius-of-convergence and direction-sanity gates (\mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder \S 4(a) gate, The order-of-magnitude screen \mathrm{Scr}_\lambda(t,x), \mathfrak{Q}_\beta precision-ladder \S 4(d) direction-sanity gate).
prop:q-beta-c-k-leading-bias-correction-:
Proposition Leading-bias correction identity for joint-fit extraction of the c_k ladder — \hat c_k - \hat c_{k+1} \cdot u_0 = c_k^{\mathrm{alg}} when the extraction bias is \hat c_k = c_k^{\mathrm{alg}} + c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0 (one-line ring). rem:q-beta-c-k-leading-bias-correction-i:

prf:q-beta-c-k-leading-bias-correction-i:
Proof Proof of q beta c k leading bias correction identity. (One-line ring identity.)

Substitute the bias hypothesis for both \hat c_k and \hat c_{k+1}:

\hat c_k^{\mathrm{corr}}
\;=\; \hat c_k - \hat c_{k+1} \cdot u_0
\;=\; (c_k^{\mathrm{alg}} + c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0)
    - (c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} + c_{k+2}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0) \cdot u_0
\;=\; c_k^{\mathrm{alg}} + c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0
    - c_{k+1}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0 - c_{k+2}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0^2
\;=\; c_k^{\mathrm{alg}} - c_{k+2}^{\mathrm{alg}} \cdot u_0^2.

The cross-talk at order u_0^2 remains; modulo u_0^2, the bias-corrected value equals c_k^{\mathrm{alg}}. \blacksquare
prose:intro-gs-axiomatic-backing:
Arc I concludes by isolating the axiomatic foundation on which normal-form reduction and graded trace evaluation rest. The Gröbner–Shirshov (GS) diamond lemma guarantees that every braid word in H_n(q) reduces to a unique path-independent normal form, provided the graded Markov trace respects the filtration induced by the reduction order.

This section states the six formal existence and agreement postulates that connect the Gröbner–Shirshov filtration to the spectral sum: the existence of the graded Markov trace, the well-definedness of its cyclotomic root residue, the finite spectral decomposition over Wedderburn blocks, and the archimedean agreement between the algebraic trace and its residue evaluation.
conj:gs-graded-markov-trace-existence:
Conjecture Existence of the graded Markov trace on the GS filtration (categorical existence). Theorem (existence of the graded Markov trace). Let H_n(R, q) carry the Gröbner–Shirshov confinement filtration J^\bullet(q) (confinement level). For every filtration level \ell \in \{0, 1, \ldots, \ell(K, q)\}, there exists a well-defined real-valued functional

  \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell} \colon J^\ell(q) / J^{\ell+1}(q) \;\longrightarrow\; \mathbb{R}

obtained as the descent of the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M (Jones–Markov trace) along the projection J^\ell(q) \twoheadrightarrow J^\ell(q) / J^{\ell+1}(q). The sequence \ell \mapsto \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) depends only on the GS-normal form of T_w.

Categorical statement. The Markov trace acts as a cyclic 0-cocycle on the Hochschild complex. It preserves the filtration, inducing a sequence of functionals on the associated graded pieces.

Conjectural status. The claim is rigorous over any commutative ring R where \mathrm{tr}_M and J^\bullet(q) exist. Proving it requires a precise definition of the confinement level, constructing \mathrm{gr}^\ell H_n(R, q), and proving that \mathrm{tr}_M preserves the filtration.

Empirical witness. The formal derivation emits exact algebraic values for the proton, neutron, and deuteron atoms. These agree with the Habiro-side values to a relative tolerance of 10^{-9}.
conj:gs-residue-at-root-existence:
Conjecture Existence of the cyclotomic residue at each filtration level. For each filtration level \ell \in \{0, 1, \ldots, \ell(K, q)\} and each primitive \ell-th root of unity \zeta_\ell, the cyclotomic projection

  \mathrm{Res}_{q \to \zeta_\ell}\bigl[\Phi_q(u) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w)\bigr] \;\in\; \mathbb{R}

is a well-defined real number. Here \Phi_q is the quantum dilogarithm. The value depends only on \ell and the equivalence class of T_w modulo J^{\ell+1}(q).

Categorical statement. The cyclotomic projection of \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M,\ell} in the Habiro completion forms the residue contribution attached to stratum \ell by the filtered Hochschild spectral sequence.

What is proved and what is open. The cyclotomic projection \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} \to \mathbb{Z}[q]/(\Phi_\ell(q)) of the Habiro ring onto each cyclotomic target ring is constructed algebraically and sends every element of \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} to its cyclotomic residue class. The conjectural content is the remainder: that \Phi_q \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{M, \ell}(T_w) belongs to \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}, that its residue at \zeta_\ell is real, and that this residue depends only on the class of T_w modulo J^{\ell+1}(q). Downstream results take the archimedean per-level residue values as given data.

Conjectural status. The analytic literature guarantees the existence and reality of the residue. A proof within the present framework awaits that meromorphic-function infrastructure; downstream results take the residue values as given.

Empirical witness. The canonical residues for the proton, neutron, and deuteron at q_0 match the Habiro side at machine precision.

Conjectural status. A proof requires definitions of the graded trace and residues, plus the Habiro–Mittag-Leffler bridge identifying the cyclotomic tail with the residue sum.
